passage:
"Nani, Nani!" Zeenat toddled in holding a wooden duck.
"What have you got, jaan?" asked Tanuja Nani.
"Duck! Look!" Zeenat pushed it into her lap.
"Such a fine duck!"
Zeenat held half her biscuit to Nani's mouth. "You eat."
"For me? Thank you, my love."
Then Zeenat bumped her head on the table leg, wailed and reached up both arms. Nani lifted her and rocked. Soon Zeenat wriggled down and went back to the duck.

qa.q: What toy did Zeenat show Tanuja Nani?
qa.a: A wooden duck.

qa.q: What does Zeenat reaching up both arms after bumping her head suggest she expects?
qa.a: She expects Nani to pick her up and comfort her, because she trusts Nani to be there.

qa.q: Which moment shows Nani's comfort working, and what could Nani keep doing?
qa.a: After Nani rocked her, Zeenat soon wriggled down and went back to the duck. Nani can keep giving quick, warm comfort so Zeenat feels safe to play again.

qa.q: What is it like for Tanuja Nani when Zeenat holds half the biscuit to her mouth?
qa.a: It is likely touching for Nani, a small gift of trust and love from the toddler ❤️

grounding: A reliably comforted toddler shows a toy, shares food and seeks a hug from a trusted grandmother, then goes back to play.

passage:
Daycare note, Tuesday. Arnab (2 years). Written by Gopika.
Arrived teary and came straight to me for a long hug. At snack time he pushed an apple slice into my hand. Twice he brought me the red truck just to show it, waited for my "Wow!" and ran back. Woke from nap upset and settled quickly on my lap.
Next: I'll keep greeting him at the gate this week and tell his mother how quickly he settles now 🙂

qa.q: What did Arnab bring Gopika twice?
qa.a: The red truck, just to show it.

qa.q: Why do you think Arnab waited for Gopika's "Wow!" before running back?
qa.a: He wanted Gopika to share his excitement, and the reply made him feel safe and confident enough to go back and play.

qa.q: What is wise about Gopika's plan to greet Arnab at the gate?
qa.a: Being the same warm person every morning keeps his comfort reliable, which is what lets him settle and explore.

qa.q: How might Arnab's mother feel reading that he settles quickly now?
qa.a: She would probably feel relieved that he trusts his caregiver and manages well away from home.

grounding: A toddler who trusts his caregiver hugs Gopika, shares his apple and shows off his toy, building early closeness.

passage: In the courtyard of their village house, Sonali was sorting wheat when little Mehak, not yet two, waddled over with a fistful of puffed rice. She pushed a few grains into her mother's mouth and laughed. A goat bleated at the gate. Mehak froze, then ran to bury her face in Sonali's dupatta. Sonali stroked her back and hummed. Soon Mehak peeked out, fetched her clay whistle and held it up high for her mother to see.

qa.q: What did Mehak push into her mother's mouth?
qa.a: A few grains of puffed rice.

qa.q: What does Mehak burying her face in Sonali's dupatta suggest she feels?
qa.a: The goat startled her, and she ran to her mother because she feels safe with her and trusts her to comfort her.

qa.q: Which of Sonali's choices helped Mehak go back to playing?
qa.a: Sonali stayed calm, stroked her back and hummed instead of hurrying her, so Mehak felt safe enough to peek out and fetch her whistle.

qa.q: How might Sonali feel when Mehak holds up the clay whistle for her?
qa.a: She would likely feel warm and proud that her daughter wants to share her small treasures with her.

grounding: A toddler who is reliably comforted shares food, runs to her mother when scared and then shows her a toy.

passage: In a small flat in Malmö, Diego, two, woke from his nap crying and padded straight to Mormor Ulla at the table. She lifted him onto her lap, and he pressed his wet cheek into her cardigan until the sobs slowed. Then he wriggled down, fetched his toy tractor and held it up to her face. "Look!" At snack time he broke his rice cake in two and pushed the bigger half into her hand. "Mormor eat."

qa.q: What did Diego push into Mormor Ulla's hand at snack time?
qa.a: He pushed the bigger half of his rice cake into her hand.

qa.q: Why did Diego go straight to Mormor Ulla when he woke up crying?
qa.a: He seems to trust her to comfort him and expects her lap to be a safe place to calm down.

qa.q: How does Mormor Ulla's quick comfort help Diego?
qa.a: By lifting him onto her lap and letting him settle, she shows him closeness is safe, so he comes back to share his toy and food.

qa.q: How might Mormor Ulla feel when Diego gives her the bigger half?
qa.a: She would probably feel touched and loved, seeing his trust and affection in that small gift. 🤍

grounding: A two-year-old who is reliably comforted seeks a hug, shows his toy and shares food with his grandmother, showing early trust.

passage: I'm Shalini, and I live across the landing from little Lalremsiami, who is two. I can't know what goes on in her head, but I notice things. When her father comes up the stairs, she drops whatever she has and runs to him with her arms up. Yesterday she carried her cup of puffed rice to him and fed him one piece at a time, very seriously. When she tripped, she cried only until he picked her up.

qa.q: What did Lalremsiami carry to her father?
qa.a: She carried her cup of puffed rice to him.

qa.q: What does Lalremsiami's running with her arms up suggest about how she feels about her father?
qa.a: It suggests she trusts him and feels safe and happy with him, expecting to be picked up.

qa.q: Why does it matter that her crying stopped once her father picked her up?
qa.a: It shows his comfort works for her, and steady comfort like this builds the trust she can carry into closeness later.

qa.q: How does Shalini, watching from across the landing, seem to see this father and child?
qa.a: Shalini seems to see a warm, trusting bond, while admitting it is only a guess from outside.

grounding: A neighbour watches a two-year-old run to her father for hugs and share food with him, showing the trust built by reliable comfort.
